title: A font’s advance places the next word

steps.title: The font gives the word its advance
steps.line: The ruler measures where the following word would start.
steps.caption: These letters are EB Garamond, explicitly requested by the scene. The pen-and-ink style chooses the paper and colours. The ruler measures the text’s advance, including the space each letter leaves before the next.
steps.picture: A dimension line marked “5.88 units”; 1 label.

steps.title: Real bold and italic have their own measurements
steps.line: The words stay the same; each cut supplies its own outlines and advance.
steps.caption: Each row draws the same words at the same size. Regular, Bold and Italic are three source-font cuts, and the number at the right is that row’s advance. The page carries their captured paths, so it needs no font download or system-font match.
steps.picture: The same words in three EB Garamond cuts: Regular, advance 4.41; Bold, advance 4.85; Italic, advance 4.24. Each cut was requested and captured from its own source font.
